reason: I want to build the arm's framework, starting with the bones that meet at the elbow.
expectation: I expect the bones to form an arm framework or a basic elbow joint, though it may still need other parts.

alternatives.reason: Cartilage and fluid seem useful for smooth joint movement, but I chose the bones first.

effect: The bones provide rigid supports, but still need a joint where they can move relative to one another.
reaction: The distinction between bending bones and movement at a joint is clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it seems relevant to making smooth joint surfaces.
expectation: I expect the cartilage and fluid to form a smooth, lubricated joint surface, though I’m unsure how it will attach to the bones.

effect: The cartilage covers bone ends, and joint fluid helps them slide; the next goal is to join the framework and attach the muscles.
reaction: The explanation makes the different roles of cartilage and fluid clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it should join the joint surfaces to the bones.
expectation: I expect an arm framework with smooth surfaces at the elbow, possibly still needing ligaments and muscles.

effect: The joint surfaces let the forearm turn, but the framework still needs a source of pulling force.
reaction: The distinction between allowing movement and producing it is clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and the ligaments seem useful for holding the joint together.
expectation: I expect the ligaments to stabilize the articulated bones, with muscles still needed to move them.

effect: The ligaments hold the joint together, and the framework now has slots for both opposing muscle pulls.
reaction: The distinction between ligaments joining bones and muscles providing pulls is useful.
reason: I want to attach the bending muscles to begin filling the framework's pull slots.
expectation: I expect the bending muscles to fill the front pull slot, leaving the rear pull slot open.

alternatives.reason: The straightening muscles should also fit, but I chose to attach the bending muscles first.

effect: The front muscles pull through tendons to bend the elbow; relaxing them does not push the bones back, so the opposing muscles are still needed.
reaction: The explanation of pulling versus relaxing is useful.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should complete the opposing pulls.
expectation: I expect the straightening muscles to fill the rear pull slot, enabling the arm to straighten as well as bend.

effect: The rear muscles provide the opposing pull, and the completed pair can also steady the joint or hold a weight still. Coordination remains another job.
reaction: Holding a weight still while muscles keep pulling was a useful surprise.

mostWorthwhile.text: Attaching the opposing muscles was most worthwhile because it connected their positions and tendon pulls to bending, straightening and holding the joint steady.

leastWorthwhile.text: Joining the smooth surfaces to the bones felt predictable because it was the only offered combination, although the result clarified that a joint permits movement without producing force.

surprise.text: I was surprised that muscles can keep pulling without shortening, such as when holding a weight still.

arbitrary.text: No action felt clearly arbitrary; the ligaments and opposing muscles each had an understandable purpose in the framework.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the opposing pulls are coordinated. The completed arm gives that next question a clear purpose, though several steps here offered only one combination.
